source_description: Existing 1901 model; checked against Brassey appendix, extracts from Parliamentary Return 90, 8 July 1901
notes: Revenue attributed to Ireland, not simply collected there.
Local taxation account receipts are assigned national revenues, not a total of locally raised rates.
Irish services is an accounting allocation, not all government payments received in Ireland.
Existing balance-of-payments model partial receipt proxies of 176000 are not additional revenue here.
Other local receipts of 1064263 are not yet added to the working subtotal.
Church income is outside the 1901 fiscal-state comparison.

local.reference: Statistical Abstract for the United Kingdom 1898–1912 (1913), Cd. 7022, table 21, printed pp. 50–51 (PDF pp. 59–60)
local.verification: 1900–01 figures checked visually against scan; sum reconciles
local.treatment: Add rates to the working subtotal. Keep government contributions and loans out. Other own receipts shown separately pending classification as current resources and checks for transfers.

spending_comparison.note: Army: 21,235 troops at 110 pounds each, assumed entirely spent in Ireland. Civil range reflects unresolved central/local grant difference.
